FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A01
The two lowest default limits are easy to mix up: 25 mph belongs to business districts and 30 mph to residence districts. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty two; confusable sec08-F08. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A01
Mountain roads carry two different defaults: 20 mph on narrow, winding mountain highways and blind curves, but 40 mph on open mountain highways. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty three; confusable sec08-F07 vs sec08-F09. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A01
Signal distance depends on the road: 100 feet in urban areas, 200 feet on four-lane highways posted above 40 mph, with 3 seconds as a general rule of thumb. [A01]
Why it matters: group signaling; difficulty three; confusable sec08-F17 vs sec08-F18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A01
Driving too slowly can also be wrong: going below a posted minimum is a violation unless conditions require it. [A01]
Why it matters: group speed limits; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F04. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A02
No-parking distances differ by object: 30 feet from signals, stop signs and railroad crossings, but 15 feet from a fire hydrant. [A02]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty three; prereq sec08-F36. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A02
A manual transmission is left in low gear facing uphill but in reverse facing downhill, while an automatic simply stays in park. [A02]
Why it matters: group parking; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F34. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A02
A U-turn, a two-point turnabout and a three-point turnabout all reverse direction; the three-point version is only for narrow two-lane roads with no other option. [A02]
Why it matters: group turning; difficulty two; confusable sec08-F27 vs sec08-F28 vs sec08-F31. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A02
While waiting to turn left, stay behind the stop line or crosswalk and keep the wheels straight, rather than edging into the intersection with wheels turned. [A02]
Why it matters: group turning; difficulty two; prereq sec08-F24 and sec08-F25 and sec08-F26. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-co-s:colorado-department-of-revenue-division-:handbook:pdf-0016]

Misconception: the posted limit is always a safe speed; it is the maximum for ideal conditions only. [A01]
Misconception: a quick lane change needs no signal; failing to signal is a traffic violation. [A01]
Misconception: you may hold the hand signal through the turn; end it before turning so both hands steer. [A01]
Misconception: pulling into the intersection while waiting to turn left saves time safely; it blocks emergency vehicles and invites a collision. [A02]
Mnemonic: Busy shops mean slower than homes: the business district limit sits below the residence district limit. [A01]
Mnemonic: Uphill low, downhill reverse, brake set, key out. [A02]
Glossary: Stopping distance means the ground covered from realizing you must stop until the vehicle is stopped. [A01]
Glossary: Reduced speed zone means a signed stretch where a lower limit than usual applies. [A01]
Glossary: Turnabout means a planned maneuver to reverse direction using a driveway, alley or the width of the road. [A02]
